HARD_FAIL.description: Direct safety, data-loss, compliance, deployment, publication-boundary, or repository-write risk.

STRONG_WARNING.description: Material user, conversion, discoverability, content-governance, or operator defect requiring prompt repair.

SOFT_WARNING.description: Quality, resilience, optimization, or cleanup defect.

INFO.description: Observability or optional planning signal with no warning annotation.

releaseGates.rationale: A lockfile install failure prevents deterministic execution.
A failed production build is a deployment blocker.

checks.scope: repository governance
checks.rationale: The registry and execution matrix must cover every validator, profile, severity, entrypoint, and CI invocation rule.

checks.scope: publication state transitions
checks.rationale: Prevents premature mass publication, ambiguous scheduling, and published records retaining preview-only state.

checks.rationale: Broken inquiry wiring, worker dispatch, or success confirmation risks silent submission loss.

checks.rationale: Queue mode and generation caps protect approval boundaries; violations require prompt repair but do not block the static site build.

checks.rationale: Throttle drift increases provider instability risk but does not make the current static release unsafe.

checks.scope: publication state transitions

checks.scope: digital products and download publishing
checks.rationale: Public free and premium download routes and resource navigation contract.

checks.scope: digital products and download publishing
checks.rationale: Admin product upload, Gumroad, price, and Cloudflare binding contract.

checks.rationale: Custom cover and PDF-first-page fallback preview contract.

checks.scope: digital products API mutation safety
checks.rationale: Prevents product updates from erasing existing uploaded file URLs and prevents premium products from publishing without live checkout state.

checks.scope: citation KPI truth boundaries
checks.rationale: Modernization validator required to preserve authority-scale truth and existing client publishing sovereignty.

checks.scope: protected client editorial core
checks.rationale: Modernization validator required to preserve authority-scale truth and existing client publishing sovereignty.

checks.scope: post-2026 rolling editorial continuity without approval bypass
checks.rationale: Modernization validator required to preserve authority-scale truth and existing client publishing sovereignty.
checks.repair_rationale: The check reads data/continuity/editorial_continuity_report.json plus the continuity rows in the brief and queue files; replenish_editorial_candidates.mjs writes exactly those three artifacts at the locked cadence, and the repo editorial-continuity workflow already runs it immediately before validating.

checks.scope: full safe autonomy lifecycle and approval removal
checks.rationale: Proves the runtime is hands-off while preserving protected-fact and skip-record-continue boundaries.

checks.scope: the human release gate survives migration into the autonomy queue, and every workflow that writes that queue validates it
checks.rationale: scripts/autonomy/migrate_queue.mjs is the only writer that puts new items into data/autonomy/queue.json and it hard-coded routineApprovalRequired/publicOnlyAfterApproval to false. It predates the human release gate of 2026-08-27; when that gate landed the 15 items already in the queue were repaired to true and the writer was not, so the defect re-armed on every item migrated afterwards. process_manifest.js#requiresIndividualApproval reads exactly those flags, so false means a standing approval may release the piece to a client live site with nobody having agreed to it. The Editorial Continuity Sidecar then migrated three such items on 2026-09-01 and validated with the six-check authority-modernization profile, which did not contain autonomy-contract, so it pushed a state its own job could not see; Content Publish run 34127601153 and Social Ingestion went red on a state they did not create. autonomy-contract catches the resulting data but nothing caught the writer or the coverage hole. This drives the real migrator in a sandbox and requires the migrated item to carry both flags true, proves through the publisher own standingApprovalFor that a gated item is refused and an ungated one is swept in, and requires every workflow running a queue writer to run a profile containing autonomy-contract. Hard-fails if the migrator moves zero probes, if the live queue is empty, or if it traces zero writer workflows.

checks.scope: safe generation, repair, skip, duplicate, and cadence behavior
checks.rationale: Behavior fixtures prove the actual safety decisions rather than merely checking that files exist.

checks.scope: server-side admin sign-in, session and lockout across /admin, /agency, and digital products
checks.rationale: Proves admin auth is server-side: a client-sent hash is refused, the password signs in, repeated failures lock out, and a missing secret fails closed (503), never open.

checks.scope: agreement between what the admin page tells the client and what the publisher actually releases
checks.rationale: Runs the admin page's own approvalFor() and the publisher's standingApprovalFor() over the real manifest and asserts they agree item by item. They silently disagreed on 2026-08-29: the publisher wrote standing_approvals/scheduledThrough, the page probed standingApprovals/through, and the client was told 112 pieces awaited her OK when her June approval already covered 111. Nothing failed; the only symptom was a wrong number on a client's screen.

checks.scope: attribution and stated reason for every piece that leaves the site
checks.rationale: Runs the admin page's own groupFor()/humanDecisionFor()/whenLine() over the real manifest and asserts that every removal says why it happened and who decided it: a human decline needs a named decider and a reason, an automated removal needs a machine-written plain-language reason that names what triggered it and is actually rendered on the row. On 2026-08-29 the page showed the client a chip reading 'Revoked 54' when publication_declines.json was empty and none of the 54 carried a revokedBy or revokedReason: all 54 were an automated 2026-08-08 duplicate-consolidation pass (>=0.85 similarity, duplicate titles, editorialContentRewritten:false) that 301-redirected each page to the article it duplicated. The reason existed only in a search-engineering report, so the page filled the silence with a word that attributed 54 removals to a decision she never made. It also asserts both write paths -- worker contentTakeDown() and the consolidation migration -- refuse to record a removal with no reason, that no client filter label asserts a choice she may not have made, and it hard-fails if it examines zero items rather than passing on an empty loop.

checks.scope: post-publication email, accepted-output freeze, and rollback
checks.rationale: Proves the client explanation request and reversible accepted-content lifecycle exist.

checks.scope: sandboxed end-to-end draft, admission, cadence, rendering, manifest, freeze, and receipt journey
checks.rationale: Proves the actual autonomous lifecycle in an isolated filesystem without allowing validator implementation details to redefine the product.

checks.scope: sandboxed bounded repair, clean reanalysis, pre/post accepted-output freeze, and exact rollback
checks.rationale: Proves self-healing is reversible and bounded rather than merely checking for a repair script.

checks.scope: published page copy under pages/
checks.rationale: External-agent build directives (FILEPATH:, || CURRENT/MISSING/EDIT:, citation-ready update text) must never reach a published page, least of all the direct-answer block an answer engine extracts.

checks.scope: items that must be approved one at a time are never covered by a standing approval
checks.rationale: Six finished guides were held out of the client's June 2026 standing approval by being scheduled into 2027, past the window's 2026-12-31 end date. It worked, and it delayed pages answering searches people were making in August by four to five months, for a requirement that has nothing to do with when a piece runs. The requirement now lives on the item as requiresIndividualApproval (or the autonomy queue's routineApprovalRequired / publicOnlyAfterApproval) and both implementations must honour it: the publisher's standingApprovalFor()/loadApprovedIds() and the admin page's approvalFor(). This runs both over the real manifest and then simulates a publish run at each gated item's own scheduled moment, asserting it releases nothing. Hard-fails if no item carries the flag, which is the most likely way the gate would be lost.

checks.scope: work whose own record says it awaits the client reaches the client
checks.rationale: Five finished guides sat at status 'draft' with scheduledAt null and the note 'Awaiting client review'. groupFor() called every non-approved item 'draft', 'draft' was not in CLIENT_GROUPS, and both renderReview() and renderBrowse() dropped them - so five pieces that said in their own record they were waiting on the client were invisible on the one screen where she decides, with nothing failing and nothing warning. This runs the page's own groupFor() over fixtures reproducing that exact shape and asserts it now reaches a client group that has a filter chip, a status option, a row label and a place in the review panel - while unfinished, mid-generation drafts stay out, because filling her queue with half-written work is not the fix either. It also pins the five PR #16 filter chips and refuses authorship language in client copy, since none of this content is written by her.

checks.scope: every release since the human gate was sealed names who made it
checks.rationale: The release gate stops crons and generators publishing to a client's live site; it does not stop the site owner, who published five localized landing pages directly on 2026-08-29. What must never happen is that release being written into data/admin/publication_approvals.json as the client's decision, because one fabricated line makes the whole audit trail worthless. This asserts every item published on or after the gate's sealed_on date is under exactly one of two rules - released on a named client approval, or recorded in ownerPublication with the publisher named, a reason given and the absence of client approval stated - and that no owner publication carries the client's name. Pre-gate releases are out of scope by design. Hard-fails if nothing post-gate exists to examine.

checks.scope: a schedule-triggered lane proves the newest published item is actually live, and its verifier is not inert
checks.rationale: Content Publish pushes its release commit with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub triggers no workflow from a GITHUB_TOKEN push, so Postdeploy Smoke and Build - both on: push - never run after the daily cron. Cloudflare Pages deploys anyway because it watches the branch, which is why the site is fine and why the gap was invisible: if a deploy fails, the manifest says an item is published, the URL 404s, and nothing alerts anyone. The fix cannot be push-triggered, because push is exactly what does not fire. This asserts a scheduled lane exists, runs after the publish cron every day, and invokes scripts/verification/verify_published_release.mjs - and then drives that verifier's own check() with seven synthetic scenarios, one healthy and six broken, so a verifier rewritten to pass everything goes red here. Hard-fails on zero workflows or zero scenarios.

checks.scope: worker/_worker.js serveStatic/isEdgeCacheable edge cache and the build-id stamp in dist/_worker.js
checks.rationale: Until 21 Oct 2026 every HTML request went worker -> ASSETS uncached (cf-cache-status DYNAMIC, 200-320 ms TTFB, Ahrefs Slow page). The worker now edge-caches static GET/HEAD on www keyed by a build id; this runs the real worker with a fake cache and requires MISS then HIT, the origin's browser Cache-Control, no caching of API/admin/forms/POST/query/non-200, the apex 301 first, and a stamped build id.

checks.scope: config/llm_routing.json, scripts/llm/free_router.mjs, every script that reaches a model provider, every workflow, docs/cost/zero-paid-llm.md and CLAUDE.md
checks.rationale: Owner policy 11 Oct 2026: nothing paid. Until 26 Oct 2026 this repo had no routing config and no router: scripts/autonomy/lib/llm_provider.mjs POSTed to whatever secrets.LLM_API_URL and secrets.LLM_MODEL named, and the daily agency-seo-monitor schedule ran OpenRouter's per-request-billed web plugin pinned to openai/gpt-4o-mini. Search Readiness items i3 and i10. This fails on a non-$0 model, an undated snapshot, a script calling a provider outside the router, a probe lane with a schedule or without confirm_paid, a scheduled workflow naming a paid model or passing a non-router key, or the written rule going missing from the doc or CLAUDE.md.

checks.scope: scripts/publishing/write_calendar_slots.mjs: the shared search-loop engine's writer replaces queued calendar posts slot for slot before release
checks.rationale: Owner ruling 3 Nov 2026: every queued Resources post is written by the engine's writer in page shape (answer first, question headings, FAQ + FAQPage, specific sources, Monika Hicks, LCSW byline, real publish date) at under 30% shared with any live page; the 58 queued posts were template clones sharing 55-98% with live pages. Runs the real writer on a fixture of real pages with a stub engine. Replaces the redraft-lane guard (redraft_held.mjs retired).
